blocks.explanation:
Formula \(a_n = 4 + 3n\) ek machine ki tarah hai: position \(n\) dalo, us jagah ki term nikal aati hai.
Find kya karna hai? Position \(n + 1\) aur position \(2n\) wali terms.
Plan: formula mein \(n\) ki jagah pehle \(n + 1\) (bracket ke saath), phir \(2n\) rakh kar simplify karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = 4 + 3n\)
Humein find karna hai: \(a_{n+1}\) aur \(a_{2n}\).
Tareeqa: Neeche likha hua chhota number (subscript) batata hai ke formula mein \(n\) ki jagah kya rakhna hai. Jo bhi subscript ho, poore formula mein har \(n\) ki jagah wohi aayega.

\(a_{n+1}\) nikalein
\[a_{n+1} = 4 + 3(n + 1)\]
\[= 4 + 3n + 3\]
\[= 3n + 7\]
Kyun: Bracket zaroori hai kyunke 3 poori position \(n + 1\) ko multiply karta hai, sirf \(n\) ko nahi. Bracket kholne par \(3n + 3\) bana, phir \(4 + 3 = 7\) jama kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(a_{n+1}\) aur \(a_n + 1\) mein bara farq hai. \(a_n + 1 = 3n + 5\) hota hai (term mein 1 jama), jabke \(a_{n+1} = 3n + 7\) agli position ki term hai.

\(a_{2n}\) nikalein
\[a_{2n} = 4 + 3(2n)\]
\[= 4 + 6n\]
Kyun: Is dafa \(n\) ki jagah \(2n\) rakha. \(3 \times 2n = 6n\). Yeh position \(n\) ki dugni jagah wali term hai, term ka dugna nahi.

Tasdeeq: ek number rakh kar
\(n = 1\) lein: \(a_2 = 4 + 3(2) = 10\) aur \(3(1) + 7 = 10 \;\checkmark\)
\(n = 2\) lein: \(a_4 = 4 + 12 = 16\) aur \(4 + 6(2) = 16 \;\checkmark\)
Kyun: Algebra ka jawab check karne ka sab se aasaan tareeqa hai ke koi chhota number rakh kar dono taraf ki value milayein. Dono jagah barabar aaya, to jawab sahi hai.
